text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least 32 people have drowned in the north of Namibia so far this year following exceptionally heavy rains and storms. At least 12 children under the age of seven were among the victims.

- The Ministry of Mines and Energy introduced unleaded petrol to Namibia on Friday. The 95 octane unleaded fuel will be available on Namibia's main routes from April 16 costing two cents more per litre than the leaded petrol currently available.

- The government and Namport signed an onlending agreement on Friday providing the Namibian Ports Authority with a soft loan of approximately 30 million Namibian dollars for structural improvements of the country's deep water harbour at Walvis Bay. The loan was granted to Namibia by the German Development Bank (KfW) at an interest rate of two percent with a maturity of 30 years including a grace period of 10 years.
